newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stamps reinstate Queen's head for a day.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stamps reinstate Queen's head for a day.

text.p: The Hong Kong Post Office will reinstate the Queen's head on a set of stamps for just one day, the last day of British rule in the territory, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Saturday.
The HK$5 (US$0.64) sheet bearing various crowns, including that of the current Queen, will be issued on June 30 and can only be legally used on that day, the South China Morning Post said.
At midnight, the stamps will be unusable as Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule, ending more than 150 years of London rule.
But the newspaper quoted a Post Office spokesman as saying the stamps could be exchanged at post office counters for crownless stamps of the same value during July.
Hong Kong is purging icons of British rule as it zeroes in on the handover. Stamps and new coins no longer show the Queen's head and many clubs have dropped their "royal" prefixes.
The government on Thursday invited bids for 27 red cast iron mail boxes, replete with the British crown insignia and royal monogram.
